title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and charged in North Dakota with four theft counts and four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information after Fargo police allegedly relied on an AI facial recognition system. She spent about six months in jail, first in Tennessee and then North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records that placed her in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud happened. She was released on Christmas Eve.

Lipps has sued the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10m. The lawsuit claims the facial recognition match came from a fake ID and a social media photo, that she did not resemble the suspect, and that she had never been to North Dakota. It also alleges lack of police policy, training, and supervision. Fargo does not comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit is pending.
